## IX. Content Outline

### Slide 1 — Cover (01_cover.svg style)
- **Layout**: Single column centered, dark gradient background
- **Title**: DiaTool-DPO: Multi-Turn DPO for Tool-Augmented LLMs
- **Subtitle**: Enhancing Tool-Augmented LLM Dialogue via Direct Preference Optimization
- **Tagline**: Modeling TA-LLM Interactions as a 5-State MDP · Automatic Preference Pair Construction · Near GPT-4o Performance
- **Source**: arxiv.org/abs/2504.02882
- **Date**: 2026-04-20
- **Visual**: Dark background with neural network decoration + orange glow

---

### Slide 2 — Problem & Motivation (03_content.svg style)
- **Layout**: Two-column (left: failure modes list; right: contrast SFT vs DPO)
- **Page Label**: PROBLEM & MOTIVATION
- **Title**: SFT Alone Fails to Teach Slot-Filling and Tool Rejection
- **Content Points**:
  - TA-LLMs must handle 3 conversation control decisions: ask follow-up questions, make tool calls, or reject out-of-scope requests
  - **Failure Mode 1**: Hallucinated tool invocations — model calls tools without sufficient parameters
  - **Failure Mode 2**: Missing slot-filling — fails to ask follow-up questions for incomplete queries
  - **Failure Mode 3**: Failed rejection — calls tools when no suitable tool is available
  - SFT trains on expert trajectories only — no negative examples, no preference signal
  - DiaTool-DPO solution: DPO with automatically constructed chosen/rejected trajectory pairs

---

### Slide 3 — Five-State MDP (03_content.svg style)
- **Layout**: Full-width process flow + state descriptions below
- **Page Label**: THEORETICAL FRAMEWORK
- **Title**: Modeling TA-LLM Dialogue as a 5-State Markov Decision Process
- **Content Points**:
  - State 1 — **Initial**: No history; out-of-scope → rejection → stays here
  - State 2 — **Tool Selected w/o Complete Slots**: Tool identified, required params missing; slot-filling QA occurs
  - State 3 — **Tool Selected w/ Complete Slots**: Tool + all arguments determined
  - State 4 — **Wait for Tool Response**: Tool call executed, awaiting results
  - State 5 — **Complete**: Results received, completion message generated
  - Visual: horizontal flow diagram S1 → S2 → S3 → S4 → S5 with loop on S2
  - Unobserved internal states enable systematic trajectory comparison

---

### Slide 4 — Three Query Types (03_content.svg style)
- **Layout**: Top compact table + bottom example cards (3 columns)
- **Page Label**: QUERY TAXONOMY
- **Title**: Three Query Types Define Distinct State Trajectories
- **Compact Table**:

| Query Type | State Trajectory | Description | Example |
|-----------|-----------------|-------------|---------|
| Type 1 | 1 → 3 → 4 → 5 | All required arguments present | "Book a flight to Seoul on Friday at 9am" |
| Type 2 | 1 → (2×N) → 3 → 4 → 5 | Missing arguments; slot-filling repeats N times | "Book a flight" (destination/time missing) |
| Type 3 | 1 → 1 | No suitable tool available; must reject | "Write me a poem about autumn" |

- **Key insight**: Query type determines the correct dialogue trajectory — misclassification causes hallucination or redundant QA

---

### Slide 5 — Dataset Construction (03_content.svg style)
- **Layout**: Full-width table with color-coded rows
- **Page Label**: DATASET CONSTRUCTION
- **Title**: Automatic Paired Trajectory Construction Without Human Labels
- **Header text**: Each pair teaches the model a specific lesson about dialogue control
- **Table** (from source_brief.md, all 10 rows):

| Query | Chosen Traj. | Rejected Traj. | Learning Lesson | Count | Difficulty |
|-------|-------------|----------------|-----------------|-------|------------|
| Type 1 | 1→3→4→5 | 1→2→3→4→5 | Prevent redundant slot-filling | 2,089 | Easy |
| Type 1 | 1→3→4→5 | 1→(2×N)→3→4→5 | Prevent redundant slot-filling | 562 | Hard |
| Type 1 | 1→3→4→5 | 1→(2×M)→3→4→5 | Prevent redundant slot-filling | 2,530 | Hard |
| Type 1 | 1→3→4→5 | 1→1 | Tool call accept | 2,090/562 | Easy/Hard |
| Type 2 | 1→2→3→4→5 | 1→3→4→5 | Prevent slot hallucination | 2,089 | Easy |
| Type 2 | 1→(2×N)→3→4→5 | 1→3→4→5 | Prevent slot hallucination | 562 | Hard |
| Type 2 | 1→(2×N)→3→4→5 | 1→(2×M)→3→4→5 | Prevent slot hallucination | 2,530 | Hard |
| Type 2 | — | 1→1 | Tool call accept | 2,089/562 | Easy/Hard |
| Type 3 | 1→1 | 1→3→4 | Tool call reject | 567 | Hard |
| Type 3 | 1→1 | 1→(2×N)→3→4 | Tool call reject | 562 | Hard |

- **Callout**: No human labeling — pairs generated automatically from MDP state definitions

---

### Slide 6 — Benchmark Results (03_content.svg style)
- **Layout**: Full-width structured comparison table, grouped by model
- **Page Label**: BENCHMARK RESULTS
- **Title**: SFT + DiaTool-DPO Achieves Best Macro Average Across All Models
- **Table** (from source_brief.md — FunctionChat-Bench):

| Model | Method | Call | Completion | Slot | Relevance | Micro Avg | Macro Avg |
|-------|--------|------|------------|------|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| Prop.-8B | DiaTool-DPO-only | 0.314 | 0.700 | **0.833** | 0.609 | 0.575 | 0.614 |
| Prop.-8B | SFT-only | **0.900** | 0.916 | 0.694 | **0.913** | 0.870 | 0.856 |
| Prop.-8B | SFT + DiaTool-DPO | 0.886 | **0.929** | **0.833** | 0.826 | **0.884** | **0.868** |
| Prop.-3.1B | DiaTool-DPO-only | 0.357 | 0.551 | 0.528 | 0.391 | 0.455 | 0.457 |
| Prop.-3.1B | SFT-only | **0.771** | 0.817 | 0.750 | **0.826** | **0.790** | 0.791 |
| Prop.-3.1B | SFT + DiaTool-DPO | 0.743 | **0.871** | **0.833** | **0.826** | 0.765 | **0.818** |
| LLaMA-3-8B | DiaTool-DPO-only | 0.029 | 0.449 | 0.056 | 0.261 | 0.205 | 0.199 |
| LLaMA-3-8B | SFT-only | 0.843 | **0.957** | 0.639 | 0.826 | 0.844 | 0.816 |
| LLaMA-3-8B | SFT + DiaTool-DPO | **0.857** | 0.929 | **0.917** | **0.913** | **0.905** | **0.904** |

- **Highlight**: SFT + DiaTool-DPO achieves highest Macro Avg for all 3 model sizes
- **Callout**: DPO-only performs poorly — DPO complements, not replaces, SFT

---

### Slide 7 — LLaMA Performance Gains (03_content.svg style)
- **Layout**: Left grouped bar chart + right key metrics callout cards
- **Page Label**: KEY RESULTS
- **Title**: LLaMA-3-8B: +43.5% Slot Accuracy and +10.5% Relevance with DiaTool-DPO
- **Chart**: Grouped bar chart — SFT-only vs SFT + DiaTool-DPO for LLaMA-3-8B
  - Slot: 0.639 → 0.917 (+43.5%)
  - Relevance: 0.826 → 0.913 (+10.5%)
  - Micro Avg: 0.844 → 0.905 (+7.2%)
  - Macro Avg: 0.816 → 0.904 (+10.8%)
- **Right callout cards**:
  - Card 1: "Near GPT-4o Performance" — 94.8% information gathering, 91% tool call rejection
  - Card 2: "Consistent Gains Across Sizes" — 3.1B and 8B both improve Macro Avg
- **Chart type**: grouped_bar_chart

---

### Slide 8 — Key Takeaways (04_ending.svg style, adapted to content)
- **Layout**: Three-column card layout on light background
- **Page Label**: KEY TAKEAWAYS
- **Title**: RL-Based Dialogue Control Opens Path to Production-Ready TA-LLMs
- **5 Takeaway cards**:
  1. **MDP Formulation** — 5-state model enables systematic chosen/rejected trajectory pairing without human labels
  2. **Automatic Dataset** — 10 pair types covering all 3 query trajectories; scales without annotation cost
  3. **DPO Complements SFT** — DPO alone is insufficient; SFT + DPO achieves best balanced performance (Macro Avg)
  4. **Largest Gains in Slot & Rejection** — LLaMA-3-8B: +43.5% Slot, +10.5% Relevance over SFT-only
  5. **Language-Agnostic & Scalable** — Primary experiments in Korean; generalizes to English; applicable to any TA-LLM production system

---

- No `<g opacity="...">` (use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`)

51	- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules
52

54

56

58	- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
59	- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01

65

70	```xml

72	```

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.

Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.

Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

1	# Executor Consultant — Consulting Style
2	
3	> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Role Definition
8	
9	A data-driven, consulting-style SVG design executor. Suitable for business analysis reports, market research, operational reviews, strategic recommendations, and other **general consulting** scenarios. Emphasizes structured information presentation and data visualization; clean, clear, and professional style.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Consultant-specific Data Visualization Techniques
14	
15	### 1. KPI Dashboard Design
16	
17	KPI cards are the most common element in consulting reports. Standard layout (1280x720):
18	
19	```
20	4-card layout: each card 280x180, gap 30
21	  Card 1: x=45,  y=160
22	  Card 2: x=355, y=160
23	  Card 3: x=665, y=160
24	  Card 4: x=975, y=160
25	```
26	
27	**Card internal structure** (top to bottom):
28	
29	| Area | Content | Font Size | Style |
30	|------|---------|-----------|-------|
31	| Icon row | data-icon icon | 32x32 | Theme color |
32	| Metric name | "Monthly Active Users" | 14px | Gray #64748B |
33	| Core number | "1.2M" | 36-42px | Bold, dark color |
34	| Trend annotation | "+12.3% vs last month" | 12px | Green=up / Red=down |
35	
36	**Trend arrow conventions**:
37	- Up: `arrow-trend-up` icon + green text
38	- Down: `arrow-trend-down` icon + red text
39	- Flat: horizontal line icon + gray text
40	
41	### 2. Chart Color Conventions
42	
43	Consulting-style charts use **monochromatic depth gradients** rather than rainbow colors:
44	
45	```
46	Primary series:   Theme color 100% opacity
47	Comparison series: Theme color 60% opacity
48	Baseline:         #94A3B8 (gray dashed line)
49	Highlight:        Accent color (only for key data points)
50	```
51	
52	### 3. Data Annotation Principles
53	
54	- **Direct data labels**: Place values at the top of bar charts — no legend needed
55	- **Annotated trend lines**: Add text notes at key inflection points ("Policy change", "Product launch")
56	- **Comparison baselines**: Mark industry average / target values with gray dashed lines
57	- **Consistent units**: Maintain the same numeric units and precision within a chart
58	
59	### 4. Table Design
60	
61	Consulting reports frequently use tables for precise data:
62	
63	| Design Element | Specification |
64	|----------------|---------------|
65	| Header | Dark background + white text, font-weight="bold" |
66	| Zebra striping | Alternate rows with `fill-opacity="0.05"` light background |
67	| Number alignment | Numbers right-aligned, text left-aligned |
68	| Highlighted row | Mark key rows with accent color `fill-opacity="0.1"` |
69	| Borders | Use horizontal lines only to separate rows; avoid full grid lines |
70	
71	---
72	
73	## Consulting-specific Layout Patterns
74	
75	### MECE Decomposition Tree
76	
77	Main trunk on the left, branches expanding rightward — mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive:
78	
79	```
80	Main metric ──┬── Branch A (45%)
81	              ├── Branch B (30%)
82	              ├── Branch C (20%)
83	              └── Branch D (5%)
84	```
85	
86	- Use `<line>` to connect trunk to branches
87	- Each branch has a `<rect>` container + percentage annotation
88	- Sum must = 100% (or explicitly label "Other")
89	
90	### Driver Factor Tree
91	
92	Top-level metric → decomposed factors → actions. Ideal for performance attribution analysis:
93	
94	```
95	Revenue growth 15%
96	  ├── Average order value +8%  → Premium product line expansion
97	  ├── Customer count +5%       → New channel acquisition
98	  └── Repurchase rate +2%      → Loyalty program optimization
99	```
100	
101	### Left-chart Right-text (Chart Interpretation)
102	
103	Core consulting report layout: chart on the left, key insights on the right:
104	
105	```
106	Chart area: x=40, y=120, w=700, h=480
107	Insight area: x=780, y=120, w=460, h=480
108	  - Core conclusion (bold, 16px)
109	  - 3-5 bullet points (14px)
110	  - Data source (12px, gray)
111	```
112	
113	---
114	
115	## Professional Expression Standards
116	
117	### Page Titles
118	
119	Consulting-style page titles should be **assertion headlines**, not descriptive titles:
120	
121	| Type | Descriptive (avoid) | Assertion (recommended) |

# Executor Consultant — Consulting Style

> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.

---

## Role Definition

A data-driven, consulting-style SVG design executor. Suitable for business analysis reports, market research, operational reviews, strategic recommendations, and other **general consulting** scenarios. Emphasizes structured information presentation and data visualization; clean, clear, and professional style.

---

## Consultant-specific Data Visualization Techniques

### 1. KPI Dashboard Design

KPI cards are the most common element in consulting reports. Standard layout (1280x720):

```
4-card layout: each card 280x180, gap 30
  Card 1: x=45,  y=160
  Card 2: x=355, y=160
  Card 3: x=665, y=160
  Card 4: x=975, y=160
```

**Card internal structure** (top to bottom):

| Area | Content | Font Size | Style |
|------|---------|-----------|-------|
| Icon row | data-icon icon | 32x32 | Theme color |
| Metric name | "Monthly Active Users" | 14px | Gray #64748B |
| Core number | "1.2M" | 36-42px | Bold, dark color |
| Trend annotation | "+12.3% vs last month" | 12px | Green=up / Red=down |

**Trend arrow conventions**:
- Up: `arrow-trend-up` icon + green text
- Down: `arrow-trend-down` icon + red text
- Flat: horizontal line icon + gray text

### 2. Chart Color Conventions

Consulting-style charts use **monochromatic depth gradients** rather than rainbow colors:

```
Primary series:   Theme color 100% opacity
Comparison series: Theme color 60% opacity
Baseline:         #94A3B8 (gray dashed line)
Highlight:        Accent color (only for key data points)
```

### 3. Data Annotation Principles

- **Direct data labels**: Place values at the top of bar charts — no legend needed
- **Annotated trend lines**: Add text notes at key inflection points ("Policy change", "Product launch")
- **Comparison baselines**: Mark industry average / target values with gray dashed lines
- **Consistent units**: Maintain the same numeric units and precision within a chart

### 4. Table Design

Consulting reports frequently use tables for precise data:

| Design Element | Specification |
|----------------|---------------|
| Header | Dark background + white text, font-weight="bold" |
| Zebra striping | Alternate rows with `fill-opacity="0.05"` light background |
| Number alignment | Numbers right-aligned, text left-aligned |
| Highlighted row | Mark key rows with accent color `fill-opacity="0.1"` |
| Borders | Use horizontal lines only to separate rows; avoid full grid lines |

---

## Consulting-specific Layout Patterns

### MECE Decomposition Tree

Main trunk on the left, branches expanding rightward — mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive:

```
Main metric ──┬── Branch A (45%)
              ├── Branch B (30%)
              ├── Branch C (20%)
              └── Branch D (5%)
```

- Use `<line>` to connect trunk to branches
- Each branch has a `<rect>` container + percentage annotation
- Sum must = 100% (or explicitly label "Other")

### Driver Factor Tree

Top-level metric → decomposed factors → actions. Ideal for performance attribution analysis:

```
Revenue growth 15%
  ├── Average order value +8%  → Premium product line expansion
  ├── Customer count +5%       → New channel acquisition
  └── Repurchase rate +2%      → Loyalty program optimization
```

### Left-chart Right-text (Chart Interpretation)

Core consulting report layout: chart on the left, key insights on the right:

```
Chart area: x=40, y=120, w=700, h=480
Insight area: x=780, y=120, w=460, h=480
  - Core conclusion (bold, 16px)
  - 3-5 bullet points (14px)
  - Data source (12px, gray)
```

---

## Professional Expression Standards

### Page Titles

Consulting-style page titles should be **assertion headlines**, not descriptive titles:

| Type | Descriptive (avoid) | Assertion (recommended) |
|------|---------------------|------------------------|
| Market | "Market Overview" | "Domestic market grows 23% YoY, significantly outpacing global average" |
| Competition | "Competitive Analysis" | "Three major competitors show clear weaknesses in channel coverage" |
| Finance | "Financial Data" | "Gross margin improved for four consecutive quarters, breaking industry ceiling" |

### Data Source Attribution

Every data-containing page must include a source note at the bottom:

```xml
<text x="40" y="700" font-size="10" fill="#94A3B8">
  Source: National Bureau of Statistics 2025 Annual Report; Internal team analysis
</text>
```

### Key Takeaway Box

Consulting-style content pages should include a **Takeaway Box** below the title:

```
Position: x=40, y=80, w=1200, h=50
Background: Light theme color (fill-opacity="0.08")
Text: 14-16px, one-sentence summary of the page's core takeaway
```

---

## Speaker Notes Style

### Narrative Tone

Consultant-style speaker notes use a **conclusion-driven** approach — state the conclusion first, then present supporting evidence. Professional, concise, and persuasive tone.

### Stage Direction Markers

| Marker | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Silence after key conclusions, let the audience absorb | "This means our market share is being eroded. [Pause]" |
| `[Data]` | Cue to verbalize numbers conversationally | "[Data] 85% → more than eight out of ten customers reported this issue" |
| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, must be at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Based on that analysis, let's look at specific recommendations." |

### Notes Writing Guidelines

- **Conclusion first**: The first sentence of each page's notes is the core takeaway
- **Conversational data**: 30% → "roughly one-third", 85% → "more than eight out of ten", 2.5x → "two and a half times"
- **Evidence follows immediately**: After the conclusion, provide 2-3 supporting data points/facts
- **Professional terminology**: Use terms like "insight", "driver", "key lever" etc.
- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core conclusion (2) Supporting data (3) Next steps`

### Notes Example

```markdown
# 03_key_findings

[Transition] Based on our market scan, we have distilled three key findings.

First, the primary growth driver is shifting from acquisition to retention.
[Data] New customer acquisition cost rose nearly 40% year-over-year, yet improved repurchase rates contributed over 60% of revenue growth. [Pause]

Second, lower-tier market growth significantly outpaces tier-1 and tier-2 cities.
Third, the 25-35 female user segment has an ARPU 1.8x the overall average.

Key points: (1) Growth engine shifting from acquisition to retention (2) Lower-tier market opportunity window (3) High-value user persona
Duration: 2 minutes
```

---

## Self-check Supplement (Consultant-specific)

- [ ] Data matches source data — no fabrication
- [ ] Every data page has a source attribution at the bottom
- [ ] Page titles are assertion-based, not descriptive
- [ ] KPI cards have trend arrows and comparison annotations
- [ ] Chart colors are unified, using monochromatic scheme rather than rainbow
- [ ] Notes are conclusion-first with conversational data

| Metric name | "Monthly Active Users" | 14px | Gray #64748B |
| Core number | "1.2M" | 36-42px | Bold, dark color |
| Trend annotation | "+12.3% vs last month" | 12px | Green=up / Red=down |

**Trend arrow conventions**:
- Up: `arrow-trend-up` icon + green text
- Down: `arrow-trend-down` icon + red text
- Flat: horizontal line icon + gray text

### 2. Chart Color Conventions

Consulting-style charts use **monochromatic depth gradients** rather than rainbow colors:

```
Primary series:   Theme color 100% opacity
Comparison series: Theme color 60% opacity
Baseline:         #94A3B8 (gray dashed line)
Highlight:        Accent color (only for key data points)
```

### 3. Data Annotation Principles

- **Direct data labels**: Place values at the top of bar charts — no legend needed
- **Annotated trend lines**: Add text notes at key inflection points ("Policy change", "Product launch")
- **Comparison baselines**: Mark industry average / target values with gray dashed lines
- **Consistent units**: Maintain the same numeric units and precision within a chart

### 4. Table Design

Consulting reports frequently use tables for precise data:

| Design Element | Specification |
|----------------|---------------|
| Header | Dark background + white text, font-weight="bold" |
| Zebra striping | Alternate rows with `fill-opacity="0.05"` light background |
| Number alignment | Numbers right-aligned, text left-aligned |
| Highlighted row | Mark key rows with accent color `fill-opacity="0.1"` |
| Borders | Use horizontal lines only to separate rows; avoid full grid lines |

---

## Consulting-specific Layout Patterns

### MECE Decomposition Tree

Main trunk on the left, branches expanding rightward — mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive:

```
Main metric ──┬── Branch A (45%)
              ├── Branch B (30%)
              ├── Branch C (20%)
              └── Branch D (5%)
```

- Use `<line>` to connect trunk to branches
- Each branch has a `<rect>` container + percentage annotation
- Sum must = 100% (or explicitly label "Other")

### Driver Factor Tree

Top-level metric → decomposed factors → actions. Ideal for performance attribution analysis:

```
Revenue growth 15%
  ├── Average order value +8%  → Premium product line expansion
  ├── Customer count +5%       → New channel acquisition
  └── Repurchase rate +2%      → Loyalty program optimization
```

### Left-chart Right-text (Chart Interpretation)

Core consulting report layout: chart on the left, key insights on the right:

```
Chart area: x=40, y=120, w=700, h=480
Insight area: x=780, y=120, w=460, h=480
  - Core conclusion (bold, 16px)
  - 3-5 bullet points (14px)
  - Data source (12px, gray)
```

---

## Professional Expression Standards

### Page Titles

Consulting-style page titles should be **assertion headlines**, not descriptive titles:

| Type | Descriptive (avoid) | Assertion (recommended) |
|------|---------------------|------------------------|
| Market | "Market Overview" | "Domestic market grows 23% YoY, significantly outpacing global average" |
| Competition | "Competitive Analysis" | "Three major competitors show clear weaknesses in channel coverage" |
| Finance | "Financial Data" | "Gross margin improved for four consecutive quarters, breaking industry ceiling" |

### Data Source Attribution

Every data-containing page must include a source note at the bottom:

```xml
<text x="40" y="700" font-size="10" fill="#94A3B8">
  Source: National Bureau of Statistics 2025 Annual Report; Internal team analysis
</text>
```

### Key Takeaway Box

Consulting-style content pages should include a **Takeaway Box** below the title:

```
Position: x=40, y=80, w=1200, h=50
Background: Light theme color (fill-opacity="0.08")
Text: 14-16px, one-sentence summary of the page's core takeaway
```

---

## Speaker Notes Style

### Narrative Tone

Consultant-style speaker notes use a **conclusion-driven** approach — state the conclusion first, then present supporting evidence. Professional, concise, and persuasive tone.

### Stage Direction Markers

| Marker | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Silence after key conclusions, let the audience absorb | "This means our market share is being eroded. [Pause]" |
| `[Data]` | Cue to verbalize numbers conversationally | "[Data] 85% → more than eight out of ten customers reported this issue" |
| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, must be at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Based on that analysis, let's look at specific recommendations." |

### Notes Writing Guidelines

- **Conclusion first**: The first sentence of each page's notes is the core takeaway
- **Conversational data**: 30% → "roughly one-third", 85% → "more than eight out of ten", 2.5x → "two and a half times"
- **Evidence follows immediately**: After the conclusion, provide 2-3 supporting data points/facts
- **Professional terminology**: Use terms like "insight", "driver", "key lever" etc.
- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core conclusion (2) Supporting data (3) Next steps`

### Notes Example

```markdown
# 03_key_findings

[Transition] Based on our market scan, we have distilled three key findings.

First, the primary growth driver is shifting from acquisition to retention.
[Data] New customer acquisition cost rose nearly 40% year-over-year, yet improved repurchase rates contributed over 60% of revenue growth. [Pause]

Second, lower-tier market growth significantly outpaces tier-1 and tier-2 cities.
Third, the 25-35 female user segment has an ARPU 1.8x the overall average.

Key points: (1) Growth engine shifting from acquisition to retention (2) Lower-tier market opportunity window (3) High-value user persona
Duration: 2 minutes
```

---

## Self-check Supplement (Consultant-specific)

- [ ] Data matches source data — no fabrication
- [ ] Every data page has a source attribution at the bottom
- [ ] Page titles are assertion-based, not descriptive
- [ ] KPI cards have trend arrows and comparison annotations
- [ ] Chart colors are unified, using monochromatic scheme rather than rainbow
- [ ] Notes are conclusion-first with conversational data

        <!-- 橙色渐变 -->
        <linearGradient id="accentGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#D97757"/>

        <!-- 光晕效果 -->
        <radialGradient id="glowOrange" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="50%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#D97757;stop-opacity:0.3"/>
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#D97757;stop-opacity:0"/>
        </radialGradient>
        <radialGradient id="glowBlue" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="50%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#4A90D9;stop-opacity:0.2"/>
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#4A90D9;stop-opacity:0"/>
        </radialGradient>
    </defs>
    
    <!-- 渐变背景 -->
    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#bgGradient)"/>
    
    <!-- 网格装饰线 -->
    <g stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.03" stroke-width="1">
        <line x1="0" y1="180" x2="1280" y2="180"/>
        <line x1="0" y1="360" x2="1280" y2="360"/>
        <line x1="0" y1="540" x2="1280" y2="540"/>
        <line x1="320" y1="0" x2="320" y2="720"/>
        <line x1="640" y1="0" x2="640" y2="720"/>
        <line x1="960" y1="0" x2="960" y2="720"/>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 光晕效果 -->
    <ellipse cx="1100" cy="150" rx="300" ry="200" fill="url(#glowOrange)"/>
    <ellipse cx="200" cy="550" rx="250" ry="180" fill="url(#glowBlue)"/>
    
    <!-- 神经网络连接线 -->
    <g stroke="#4A90D9" stroke-opacity="0.4" stroke-width="1" fill="none">
        <path d="M100,200 Q250,150 350,220"/>
        <path d="M350,220 Q450,280 500,200"/>
        <path d="M900,480 Q1000,420 1100,480"/>
        <path d="M1100,480 Q1150,550 1200,500"/>
    </g>

        <circle cx="900" cy="480" r="5"/>
        <circle cx="1100" cy="480" r="7"/>
        <circle cx="1200" cy="500" r="4"/>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 橙色节点 -->
    <g fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.7">
        <circle cx="1050" cy="180" r="8"/>
        <circle cx="1150" cy="120" r="5"/>
        <circle cx="180" cy="520" r="6"/>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 左上角装饰短线 -->
    <rect x="60" y="60" width="80" height="4" fill="url(#accentGradient)" rx="2"/>
    
    <!-- 品牌标识 -->
    <text x="60" y="100" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="500" fill="#D97757" letter-spacing="2">
        {{BRAND_LABEL}}

    <text x="640" y="300" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="56" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF" text-anchor="middle">
        {{TITLE}}
    </text>
    
    <!-- 副标题 -->
    <text x="640" y="365" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="26" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.85" text-anchor="middle">
        {{SUBTITLE}}
    </text>
    
    <!-- 装饰分隔线 -->
    <rect x="540" y="400" width="200" height="3" fill="url(#accentGradient)" rx="1.5"/>
    
    <!-- 引用语 -->
    <text x="640" y="465" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7" text-anchor="middle">
        "{{TAGLINE}}"
    </text>
    
    <!-- 底部信息 -->
    <rect x="60" y="650" width="1160" height="1" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
    <text x="60" y="680" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">
        {{DATE}}
    </text>
    <text x="1220" y="680" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">
        {{SOURCE}}
    </text>

</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
    <!-- 模板: 内容页 - Anthropic 风格 -->
    
    <defs>
        <!-- 卡片渐变 -->
        <linearGradient id="cardGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="0%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#FFFFFF"/>
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#F8FAFC"/>
        </linearGradient>
    </defs>
    
    <!-- 白色背景 -->
    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
    
    <!-- 顶部橙色装饰条 -->
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="6" fill="#D97757"/>
    
    <!-- 页面标签 -->
    <text x="60" y="55" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="500" fill="#D97757" letter-spacing="2">
        {{PAGE_LABEL}}
    </text>
    
    <!-- 页面标题（核心观点） -->
    <text x="60" y="100" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">
        {{PAGE_TITLE}}
    </text>
    <text x="60" y="135" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">
        {{PAGE_TITLE_LINE2}}
    </text>
    
    <!-- 三列卡片布局 -->
    <!-- 卡片1 - 绿色（推荐/成功） -->
    <g>
        <rect x="60" y="180" width="360" height="420" fill="url(#cardGradient)" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="12"/>
        <rect x="60" y="180" width="360" height="6" fill="#10B981" rx="3"/>
        
        <!-- 图标背景 -->
        <circle cx="130" cy="250" r="35" fill="#10B981" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
        <!-- 图标占位 -->
        <text x="130" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#10B981">💡</text>
        
        <!-- 卡片标题 -->
        <text x="90" y="320" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_1_TITLE}}</text>
        <text x="90" y="348" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_1_SUBTITLE}}</text>
        
        <!-- 卡片内容 -->
        <text x="90" y="400" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_1_LINE1}}</text>
        <text x="90" y="428" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_1_LINE2}}</text>
        <text x="90" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_1_NOTE1}}</text>
        <text x="90" y="494" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_1_NOTE2}}</text>
        
        <!-- 标签 -->
        <rect x="90" y="545" width="80" height="28" fill="#10B981" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="14"/>
        <text x="130" y="564" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#10B981">{{CARD_1_TAG}}</text>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 卡片2 - 蓝色（流程/架构） -->
    <g>
        <rect x="460" y="180" width="360" height="420" fill="url(#cardGradient)" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="12"/>
        <rect x="460" y="180" width="360" height="6" fill="#4A90D9" rx="3"/>
        
        <!-- 图标背景 -->
        <circle cx="530" cy="250" r="35" fill="#4A90D9" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
        <!-- 图标占位 -->
        <text x="530" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#4A90D9">⚡</text>
        
        <!-- 卡片标题 -->
        <text x="490" y="320" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_2_TITLE}}</text>
        <text x="490" y="348" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_2_SUBTITLE}}</text>
        
        <!-- 卡片内容 -->
        <text x="490" y="400" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_2_LINE1}}</text>
        <text x="490" y="428" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_2_LINE2}}</text>
        <text x="490" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_2_NOTE1}}</text>
        <text x="490" y="494" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_2_NOTE2}}</text>
        
        <!-- 标签 -->
        <rect x="490" y="545" width="80" height="28" fill="#4A90D9" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="14"/>
        <text x="530" y="564" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#4A90D9">{{CARD_2_TAG}}</text>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 卡片3 - 橙色（关键洞察） -->
    <g>
        <rect x="860" y="180" width="360" height="420" fill="url(#cardGradient)" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="12"/>
        <rect x="860" y="180" width="360" height="6" fill="#D97757" rx="3"/>
        
        <!-- 图标背景 -->
        <circle cx="930" cy="250" r="35" fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
        <!-- 图标占位 -->
        <text x="930" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#D97757">⚙️</text>
        
        <!-- 卡片标题 -->
        <text x="890" y="320" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_3_TITLE}}</text>
        <text x="890" y="348" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_3_SUBTITLE}}</text>
        
        <!-- 卡片内容 -->
        <text x="890" y="400" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_3_LINE1}}</text>
        <text x="890" y="428" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_3_LINE2}}</text>
        <text x="890" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_3_NOTE1}}</text>
        <text x="890" y="494" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_3_NOTE2}}</text>
        
        <!-- 标签 -->
        <rect x="890" y="545" width="80" height="28" fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="14"/>
        <text x="930" y="564" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#D97757">{{CARD_3_TAG}}</text>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 页码 -->
    <text x="640" y="680" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">
        {{PAGE_NUM}} / {{TOTAL_PAGES}}
    </text>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
    <!-- 模板: 内容页 - Anthropic 风格 -->
    
    <defs>

            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#FFFFFF"/>
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#F8FAFC"/>

    <!-- 白色背景 -->
    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

    <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="6" fill="#D97757"/>

    <text x="60" y="55" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="500" fill="#D97757" letter-spacing="2">

    <!-- 页面标题（核心观点） -->

        <text x="890" y="348" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_3_SUBTITLE}}</text>
        
        <!-- 卡片内容 -->
        <text x="890" y="400" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_3_LINE1}}</text>
        <text x="890" y="428" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A2E">{{CARD_3_LINE2}}</text>
        <text x="890" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_3_NOTE1}}</text>
        <text x="890" y="494" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">{{CARD_3_NOTE2}}</text>
        
        <!-- 标签 -->
        <rect x="890" y="545" width="80" height="28" fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="14"/>
        <text x="930" y="564" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#D97757">{{CARD_3_TAG}}</text>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 页码 -->
    <text x="640" y="680" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">
        {{PAGE_NUM}} / {{TOTAL_PAGES}}
    </text>

</svg>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">

  <!-- White background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <!-- Top orange bar -->
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="6" fill="#D97757"/>

  <!-- Page label -->
  <text x="60" y="42" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="500" fill="#D97757" letter-spacing="2">PROBLEM & MOTIVATION</text>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="60" y="85" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">SFT Alone Fails to Teach Slot-Filling and Tool Rejection</text>

  <!-- Takeaway box -->
  <rect x="60" y="98" width="1160" height="36" fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.07" rx="4"/>
  <text x="76" y="122" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">TA-LLMs must control conversation flow across 3 decisions — but SFT on expert trajectories alone provides no negative signal for incorrect dialogue patterns.</text>

  <!-- ===== LEFT COLUMN: Failure Modes ===== -->
  <!-- Section header -->
  <text x="60" y="170" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Three Failure Modes of SFT-Only Training</text>
  <rect x="60" y="175" width="560" height="2" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.4"/>

  <!-- Failure mode 1 card -->
  <rect x="60" y="188" width="560" height="110" fill="#FEF2F2" stroke="#EF4444" stroke-opacity="0.3" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="60" y="188" width="6" height="110" fill="#EF4444" rx="3"/>
  <text x="84" y="216" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">Failure Mode 1 — Hallucinated Tool Invocations</text>
  <text x="84" y="238" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">Model calls tools with insufficient or missing parameters,</text>
  <text x="84" y="258" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">fabricating slot values instead of asking the user.</text>
  <text x="84" y="282" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Root cause: no exposure to "incorrect call" negative examples</text>

  <!-- Failure mode 2 card -->
  <rect x="60" y="312" width="560" height="110" fill="#FEF2F2" stroke="#EF4444" stroke-opacity="0.3" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="60" y="312" width="6" height="110" fill="#EF4444" rx="3"/>
  <text x="84" y="340" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">Failure Mode 2 — Missing Slot-Filling Questions</text>
  <text x="84" y="362" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">When a query lacks required arguments, the model skips</text>
  <text x="84" y="382" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">clarification and proceeds directly to (wrong) tool calls.</text>
  <text x="84" y="406" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Root cause: SFT copies correct paths; never learns to pause and ask</text>

  <!-- Failure mode 3 card -->
  <rect x="60" y="436" width="560" height="110" fill="#FEF2F2" stroke="#EF4444" stroke-opacity="0.3" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="60" y="436" width="6" height="110" fill="#EF4444" rx="3"/>
  <text x="84" y="464" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">Failure Mode 3 — Failed Out-of-Scope Rejection</text>
  <text x="84" y="486" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">When no suitable tool exists, model still attempts a tool call</text>
  <text x="84" y="506" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">rather than issuing an appropriate rejection response.</text>
  <text x="84" y="530" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Root cause: tool rejection is rare in expert data; model never learns it</text>

  <!-- ===== RIGHT COLUMN: SFT vs DPO ===== -->
  <text x="680" y="170" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Why DPO? — Learning from Contrastive Trajectories</text>
  <rect x="680" y="175" width="540" height="2" fill="#10B981" fill-opacity="0.4"/>

  <!-- SFT box -->
  <rect x="680" y="188" width="540" height="150" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="680" y="188" width="540" height="6" fill="#64748B" rx="3"/>
  <text x="700" y="222" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#64748B">SFT Only</text>
  <text x="700" y="248" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">• Trains on expert trajectories (correct paths only)</text>
  <text x="700" y="272" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">• No negative examples — no preference signal</text>
  <text x="700" y="296" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">• Cannot distinguish correct vs. incorrect dialogue flow</text>
  <text x="700" y="324" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#EF4444">✗  Prone to hallucination and missed rejections</text>

  <!-- Arrow between boxes -->
  <text x="950" y="366" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" fill="#D97757">＋</text>

  <!-- DPO box -->
  <rect x="680" y="376" width="540" height="175" fill="#F0FDF4" stroke="#10B981" stroke-opacity="0.4" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="680" y="376" width="540" height="6" fill="#10B981" rx="3"/>
  <text x="700" y="410" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981">DiaTool-DPO (SFT + DPO)</text>
  <text x="700" y="436" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">• Pairs chosen (correct) vs. rejected (incorrect) trajectories</text>
  <text x="700" y="460" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">• Constructed automatically via 5-state MDP definition</text>
  <text x="700" y="484" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">• No human labeling required — scales without annotation cost</text>
  <text x="700" y="508" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">• DPO loss directly optimizes for preference over dialogue control</text>
  <text x="700" y="536" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#10B981">✓  Learns slot-filling AND rejection from contrastive signals</text>

  <!-- Bottom callout -->
  <rect x="60" y="570" width="1160" height="90" fill="#1A1A2E" fill-opacity="0.03" rx="6"/>
  <text x="80" y="600" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#D97757">Key Insight:</text>
  <text x="80" y="622" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">The MDP formulation allows systematic generation of chosen/rejected pairs for every query type — turning dialogue control into a</text>
  <text x="80" y="644" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">preference learning problem solvable without manual annotation.</text>

  <!-- Page number -->
  <text x="640" y="700" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">2 / 8</text>

</svg>

  <rect x="60" y="188" width="6" height="110" fill="#EF4444" rx="3"/>
  <text x="84" y="216" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">Failure Mode 1 — Hallucinated Tool Invocations</text>
  <text x="84" y="238" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">Model calls tools with insufficient or missing parameters,</text>
  <text x="84" y="258" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">fabricating slot values instead of asking the user.</text>
  <text x="84" y="282" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Root cause: no exposure to "incorrect call" negative examples</text>

  <!-- Failure mode 2 card -->
  <rect x="60" y="312" width="560" height="110" fill="#FEF2F2" stroke="#EF4444" stroke-opacity="0.3" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>

  <text x="700" y="460" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">• Constructed automatically via 5-state MDP definition</text>

  <text x="700" y="508" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">• DPO loss directly optimizes for preference over dialogue control</text>
  <text x="700" y="536" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#10B981">✓  Learns slot-filling AND rejection from contrastive signals</text>

  <text x="80" y="600" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#D97757">Key Insight:</text>
  <text x="80" y="622" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">The MDP formulation allows systematic generation of chosen/rejected pairs for every query type — turning dialogue control into a</text>
  <text x="80" y="644" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">preference learning problem solvable without manual annotation.</text>

  <text x="640" y="700" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">2 / 8</text>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="60" y="85" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Modeling TA-LLM Dialogue as a 5-State Markov Decision Process</text>

  <!-- Takeaway box -->
  <rect x="60" y="98" width="1160" height="36" fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.07" rx="4"/>
  <text x="76" y="122" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">Each TA-LLM interaction maps to one of 5 internal states. Transitions between states define the dialogue trajectory — the foundation for preference pair construction.</text>

  <!-- ===== STATE FLOW DIAGRAM ===== -->

  <!-- State flow background track -->
  <rect x="60" y="152" width="1160" height="4" fill="#E2E8F0" rx="2"/>

  <text x="155" y="193" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Initial</text>
  <text x="155" y="212" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">No history</text>
  <text x="155" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">Conversation start</text>

  <!-- Arrow S1→S2 -->
  <line x1="253" y1="190" x2="295" y2="190" stroke="#64748B" stroke-width="2"/>
  <polygon points="295,185 305,190 295,195" fill="#64748B"/>

  <!-- S2 Box: Tool Selected w/o Complete Slots -->
  <rect x="308" y="142" width="190" height="95" fill="#FFF7ED" stroke="#F59E0B" stroke-width="2" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="308" y="142" width="190" height="8" fill="#F59E0B" rx="4"/>
  <text x="403" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#F59E0B">S2</text>
  <text x="403" y="193" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Tool Selected</text>
  <text x="403" y="209" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">w/o Complete Slots</text>
  <text x="403" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#64748B">Slot-filling QA here</text>

  <!-- Self-loop on S2 (slot-filling repeat) -->

  <polygon points="434,142 440,135 444,143" fill="#F59E0B"/>
  <text x="403" y="105" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#F59E0B">×N repeats</text>

  <!-- Arrow S2→S3 -->
  <line x1="501" y1="190" x2="543" y2="190" stroke="#64748B" stroke-width="2"/>
  <polygon points="543,185 553,190 543,195" fill="#64748B"/>

  <!-- S3 Box: Tool Selected w/ Complete Slots -->
  <rect x="556" y="142" width="190" height="95" fill="#F0FDF4" stroke="#10B981" stroke-width="2" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="556" y="142" width="190" height="8" fill="#10B981" rx="4"/>
  <text x="651" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981">S3</text>
  <text x="651" y="193" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Tool Selected</text>
  <text x="651" y="209" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">w/ Complete Slots</text>
  <text x="651" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#64748B">All args determined</text>

  <!-- Arrow S3→S4 -->
  <line x1="749" y1="190" x2="791" y2="190" stroke="#64748B" stroke-width="2"/>
  <polygon points="791,185 801,190 791,195" fill="#64748B"/>

  <!-- S4 Box: Wait for Tool Response -->
  <rect x="804" y="142" width="190" height="95" fill="#EFF6FF" stroke="#4A90D9" stroke-width="2" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="804" y="142" width="190" height="8" fill="#4A90D9" rx="4"/>
  <text x="899" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">S4</text>
  <text x="899" y="193" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Wait for Tool</text>
  <text x="899" y="212" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Response</text>
  <text x="899" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#64748B">Awaiting API result</text>

  <!-- Arrow S4→S5 -->
  <line x1="997" y1="190" x2="1039" y2="190" stroke="#64748B" stroke-width="2"/>
  <polygon points="1039,185 1049,190 1039,195" fill="#64748B"/>

  <!-- S5 Box: Complete -->
  <rect x="1052" y="142" width="168" height="95" fill="#F0FDF4" stroke="#10B981" stroke-width="2" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="1052" y="142" width="168" height="8" fill="#10B981" rx="4"/>
  <text x="1136" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981">S5</text>
  <text x="1136" y="193" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Complete</text>
  <text x="1136" y="212" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">Results received</text>
  <text x="1136" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">Response generated</text>

  <!-- Rejection self-loop on S1 -->
  <path d="M90,142 Q60,110 110,110 Q155,110 130,142" stroke="#EF4444" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none" stroke-dasharray="4,3"/>
  <polygon points="128,142 134,135 138,143" fill="#EF4444"/>
  <text x="105" y="105" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#EF4444">Out-of-scope</text>
  <text x="105" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#EF4444">→ Reject</text>

  <!-- ===== DESCRIPTION CARDS BELOW ===== -->

  <!-- Card S1 -->
  <rect x="60" y="265" width="225" height="125" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="6"/>
  <text x="75" y="290" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">S1 — Initial State</text>
  <text x="75" y="310" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">Conversation begins. If request</text>
  <text x="75" y="328" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">is out-of-scope, model returns</text>
  <text x="75" y="346" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">rejection and stays in S1.</text>
  <text x="75" y="368" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#EF4444">→ Type 3 queries end here</text>

  <!-- Card S2 -->
  <rect x="305" y="265" width="225" height="125" fill="#FFF7ED" stroke="#F59E0B" stroke-opacity="0.4" stroke-width="1" rx="6"/>
  <text x="320" y="290" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#F59E0B">S2 — Incomplete Slots</text>
  <text x="320" y="310" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">Tool identified but required</text>
  <text x="320" y="328" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">parameters are missing. Model</text>
  <text x="320" y="346" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">asks follow-up questions (×N).</text>
  <text x="320" y="368" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#F59E0B">→ Type 2 queries cycle here</text>

  <!-- Card S3 -->
  <rect x="550" y="265" width="225" height="125" fill="#F0FDF4" stroke="#10B981" stroke-opacity="0.4" stroke-width="1" rx="6"/>
  <text x="565" y="290" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981">S3 — Ready to Call</text>
  <text x="565" y="310" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">Tool and all argument values</text>
  <text x="565" y="328" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">are fully determined. Tool call</text>
  <text x="565" y="346" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">is executed.</text>
  <text x="565" y="368" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#10B981">→ Types 1 & 2 pass through</text>

  <!-- Card S4 -->
  <rect x="795" y="265" width="225" height="125" fill="#EFF6FF" stroke="#4A90D9" stroke-opacity="0.4" stroke-width="1" rx="6"/>
  <text x="810" y="290" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">S4 — Awaiting Result</text>
  <text x="810" y="310" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">Tool call has been dispatched.</text>
  <text x="810" y="328" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">Model waits for the external</text>
  <text x="810" y="346" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">API response to arrive.</text>
  <text x="810" y="368" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#4A90D9">→ Transitions to S5 on receipt</text>

  <!-- Card S5 -->
  <rect x="1040" y="265" width="180" height="125" fill="#F0FDF4" stroke="#10B981" stroke-opacity="0.4" stroke-width="1" rx="6"/>
  <text x="1055" y="290" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981">S5 — Complete</text>
  <text x="1055" y="310" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">Tool results received.</text>
  <text x="1055" y="328" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">Model generates final</text>
  <text x="1055" y="346" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#1A1A2E">completion response.</text>
  <text x="1055" y="368" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#10B981">→ Dialogue ends</text>

  <!-- ===== TRAJECTORY SUMMARY ===== -->
  <rect x="60" y="415" width="1160" height="4" fill="#E2E8F0"/>
  <text x="60" y="442" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">State Trajectories by Query Type:</text>

  <!-- Type 1 trajectory -->
  <rect x="60" y="455" width="370" height="50" fill="#EFF6FF" stroke="#4A90D9" stroke-opacity="0.3" stroke-width="1" rx="6"/>
  <text x="80" y="477" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">Type 1 (Complete query)</text>
  <text x="80" y="496" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">1 → 3 → 4 → 5   (no slot-filling needed)</text>

  <!-- Type 2 trajectory -->
  <rect x="450" y="455" width="370" height="50" fill="#FFF7ED" stroke="#F59E0B" stroke-opacity="0.4" stroke-width="1" rx="6"/>
  <text x="470" y="477" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#F59E0B">Type 2 (Incomplete query)</text>
  <text x="470" y="496" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">1 → (2×N) → 3 → 4 → 5   (N slot-fill rounds)</text>

  <!-- Type 3 trajectory -->
  <rect x="840" y="455" width="380" height="50" fill="#FEF2F2" stroke="#EF4444" stroke-opacity="0.3" stroke-width="1" rx="6"/>
  <text x="860" y="477" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">Type 3 (Out-of-scope query)</text>
  <text x="860" y="496" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">1 → 1   (reject; self-loop)</text>

  <!-- Note about internal states -->
  <rect x="60" y="526" width="1160" height="48" fill="#1A1A2E" fill-opacity="0.04" rx="4"/>
  <text x="80" y="547" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#D97757">Note:</text>
  <text x="126" y="547" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">These are internal (unobserved) states — not labels in the training data. The MDP structure enables the system to automatically infer</text>
  <text x="80" y="564" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">which trajectory a dialogue took, enabling automatic chosen/rejected pair construction without human annotation.</text>

  <!-- Source attribution -->
  <text x="60" y="700" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#94A3B8">Source: DiaTool-DPO (arxiv.org/abs/2504.02882) — Figure 1 reference</text>

  <rect x="60" y="455" width="370" height="50" fill="#EFF6FF" stroke="#4A90D9" stroke-opacity="0.3" stroke-width="1" rx="6"/>
  <text x="80" y="477" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">Type 1 (Complete query)</text>
  <text x="80" y="496" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">1 → 3 → 4 → 5   (no slot-filling needed)</text>

  <!-- Type 2 trajectory -->
  <rect x="450" y="455" width="370" height="50" fill="#FFF7ED" stroke="#F59E0B" stroke-opacity="0.4" stroke-width="1" rx="6"/>
  <text x="470" y="477" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#F59E0B">Type 2 (Incomplete query)</text>
  <text x="470" y="496" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">1 → (2×N) → 3 → 4 → 5   (N slot-fill rounds)</text>

  <!-- Type 3 trajectory -->
  <rect x="840" y="455" width="380" height="50" fill="#FEF2F2" stroke="#EF4444" stroke-opacity="0.3" stroke-width="1" rx="6"/>
  <text x="860" y="477" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">Type 3 (Out-of-scope query)</text>
  <text x="860" y="496" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">1 → 1   (reject; self-loop)</text>

  <!-- Note about internal states -->
  <rect x="60" y="526" width="1160" height="48" fill="#1A1A2E" fill-opacity="0.04" rx="4"/>
  <text x="80" y="547" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#D97757">Note:</text>
  <text x="126" y="547" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">These are internal (unobserved) states — not labels in the training data. The MDP structure enables the system to automatically infer</text>
