  <!-- White background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <!-- Top orange bar -->
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="6" fill="#D97757"/>

  <!-- Page label -->
  <text x="60" y="42" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="500" fill="#D97757" letter-spacing="2">QUERY TAXONOMY</text>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="60" y="85" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Three Query Types Define Distinct State Trajectories</text>

  <!-- Takeaway box -->
  <rect x="60" y="98" width="1160" height="36" fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.07" rx="4"/>
  <text x="76" y="122" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#1A1A2E">Query type determines the correct dialogue path. Misclassification produces hallucinated calls (Types 1&2) or missed rejections (Type 3).</text>

  <!-- ===== COMPACT TABLE ===== -->

  <!-- Table container -->
  <rect x="60" y="146" width="1160" height="200" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>

  <!-- Table header row -->
  <rect x="60" y="146" width="1160" height="42" fill="#1A1A2E" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="60" y="168" width="1160" height="20" fill="#1A1A2E"/>

  <text x="155" y="173" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Query Type</text>
  <text x="390" y="173" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">State Trajectory</text>
  <text x="640" y="173" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Description</text>
  <text x="1000" y="173" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Example User Query</text>

  <!-- Column dividers in header -->
  <line x1="260" y1="146" x2="260" y2="188" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.2" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="520" y1="146" x2="520" y2="188" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.2" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="760" y1="146" x2="760" y2="188" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.2" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- Row 1: Type 1 -->
  <rect x="60" y="188" width="1160" height="52" fill="#EFF6FF"/>
  <line x1="260" y1="188" x2="260" y2="240" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="520" y1="188" x2="520" y2="240" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="760" y1="188" x2="760" y2="240" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>

  <rect x="84" y="200" width="12" height="12" fill="#4A90D9" rx="2"/>
  <text x="106" y="212" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">Type 1</text>
  <text x="106" y="230" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">Complete query</text>

  <text x="390" y="208" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">1 → 3 → 4 → 5</text>
  <text x="390" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">No slot-filling needed</text>

  <text x="540" y="208" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">All required arguments are present in</text>
  <text x="540" y="226" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">the initial user utterance.</text>

  <text x="780" y="208" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E" font-style="italic">"Book a flight to Seoul on Friday at 9am"</text>
  <text x="780" y="226" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">(destination + date + time all provided)</text>

  <!-- Row 2: Type 2 -->
  <rect x="60" y="240" width="1160" height="54" fill="#FFFBEB"/>
  <line x1="260" y1="240" x2="260" y2="294" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="520" y1="240" x2="520" y2="294" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="760" y1="240" x2="760" y2="294" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>

  <rect x="84" y="252" width="12" height="12" fill="#F59E0B" rx="2"/>
  <text x="106" y="264" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#F59E0B">Type 2</text>
  <text x="106" y="282" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">Incomplete query</text>

  <text x="390" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">1 → (2×N) → 3 → 4 → 5</text>
  <text x="390" y="278" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">N rounds of slot-filling QA</text>

  <text x="540" y="258" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">Query lacks required arguments. Model</text>
  <text x="540" y="276" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">asks follow-up questions until slots filled.</text>

  <text x="780" y="258" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E" font-style="italic">"Book a flight"</text>
  <text x="780" y="276" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">(destination and time missing → ask user)</text>

  <!-- Row 3: Type 3 -->
  <rect x="60" y="294" width="1160" height="52" fill="#FFF1F1"/>
  <rect x="60" y="334" width="1160" height="12" fill="#FFF1F1" rx="8"/>
  <line x1="260" y1="294" x2="260" y2="346" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="520" y1="294" x2="520" y2="346" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="760" y1="294" x2="760" y2="346" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1"/>

  <rect x="84" y="306" width="12" height="12" fill="#EF4444" rx="2"/>
  <text x="106" y="318" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">Type 3</text>
  <text x="106" y="336" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">Out-of-scope query</text>

  <text x="390" y="312" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">1 → 1</text>
  <text x="390" y="332" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">Self-loop; reject and stay</text>

  <text x="540" y="312" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">No suitable tool available for request.</text>
  <text x="540" y="330" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">Tool call must be rejected.</text>

  <text x="780" y="312" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E" font-style="italic">"Write me a poem about autumn"</text>
  <text x="780" y="330" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">(no poetry tool available → reject)</text>

  <!-- ===== DETAILED CARDS ===== -->

  <!-- Card Type 1 -->
  <rect x="60" y="368" width="365" height="210" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#4A90D9" stroke-opacity="0.4" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="60" y="368" width="365" height="6" fill="#4A90D9" rx="3"/>
  <use data-icon="circle-number-1" x="76" y="382" width="22" height="22" fill="#4A90D9"/>
  <text x="108" y="400" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">Type 1 — Direct Tool Call</text>
  <text x="76" y="426" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">• User provides all required slots upfront</text>
  <text x="76" y="448" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">• Model proceeds immediately to tool call</text>
  <text x="76" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">• Shortest trajectory: S1→S3→S4→S5</text>
  <text x="76" y="498" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E" font-weight="bold">DPO Lesson:</text>
  <text x="76" y="516" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Prevent model from adding redundant</text>
  <text x="76" y="534" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">slot-filling questions when unnecessary</text>
  <text x="76" y="556" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#4A90D9">Chosen: 1→3→4→5   Rejected: 1→2→3→4→5</text>

  <!-- Card Type 2 -->
  <rect x="457" y="368" width="365" height="210" fill="#FFFDF0" stroke="#F59E0B" stroke-opacity="0.4" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="457" y="368" width="365" height="6" fill="#F59E0B" rx="3"/>
  <use data-icon="circle-number-2" x="473" y="382" width="22" height="22" fill="#F59E0B"/>
  <text x="505" y="400" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#F59E0B">Type 2 — Slot-Filling Dialogue</text>
  <text x="473" y="426" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">• User query is missing required parameters</text>
  <text x="473" y="448" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">• Model enters S2, asks questions N times</text>
  <text x="473" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">• Trajectory loops on S2 until all slots filled</text>
  <text x="473" y="498" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E" font-weight="bold">DPO Lesson:</text>
  <text x="473" y="516" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Prevent slot hallucination — model must ask,</text>
  <text x="473" y="534" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">not fabricate missing argument values</text>
  <text x="473" y="556" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#F59E0B">Chosen: 1→2×N→3→4→5   Rejected: 1→3→4→5</text>

  <!-- Card Type 3 -->
  <rect x="854" y="368" width="366" height="210" fill="#FFF5F5" stroke="#EF4444" stroke-opacity="0.4" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="854" y="368" width="366" height="6" fill="#EF4444" rx="3"/>
  <use data-icon="circle-number-3" x="870" y="382" width="22" height="22" fill="#EF4444"/>
  <text x="902" y="400" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">Type 3 — Tool Rejection</text>
  <text x="870" y="426" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">• No suitable tool exists for the request</text>
  <text x="870" y="448" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">• Model must decline and stay in S1</text>
  <text x="870" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E">• Self-loop: S1→S1 (rejection path)</text>
  <text x="870" y="498" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1A1A2E" font-weight="bold">DPO Lesson:</text>
  <text x="870" y="516" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Learn to identify when no tool matches;</text>
  <text x="870" y="534" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">reject gracefully instead of hallucinating</text>
  <text x="870" y="556" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#EF4444">Chosen: 1→1   Rejected: 1→3→4</text>

  <!-- Page number -->
  <text x="640" y="700" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">4 / 8</text>

</svg>

    <defs>
        <!-- 背景渐变 -->

            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#1A1A2E"/>

        <linearGradient id="accentGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">

        <radialGradient id="glowOrange" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="50%">

        <radialGradient id="glowBlue" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="50%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#4A90D9;stop-opacity:0.15"/>

        </radialGradient>
    </defs>
    
    <!-- 渐变背景 -->
    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#bgGradient)"/>
    
    <!-- 网格装饰线 -->
    <g stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.02" stroke-width="1">
        <line x1="0" y1="180" x2="1280" y2="180"/>

    <!-- 光晕效果 -->
    <ellipse cx="300" cy="200" rx="250" ry="180" fill="url(#glowBlue)"/>

    <!-- 神经网络连接装饰 -->

        <path d="M150,150 Q250,100 350,180"/>

        <path d="M1100,420 Q1150,500 1080,550"/>

    <!-- 节点装饰 -->

        THANK YOU
    </text>
    
    <!-- 主感谢语 -->
    <text x="640" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="52" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">
        {{THANK_YOU}}
    </text>
    
    <!-- 装饰分隔线 -->

        {{TAGLINE}}

    <text x="640" y="505" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">
        {{CONTACT_NAME}}
    </text>
    <text x="640" y="535" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7">
        {{CONTACT_EMAIL}}
    </text>
    <text x="640" y="560" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.6">
        {{CONTACT_URL}}
    </text>
    
    <!-- 底部分隔线 -->
    <rect x="60" y="640" width="1160" height="1" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
    
    <!-- 底部信息 -->

        {{DATE}}
    </text>
    <text x="1220" y="680" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">
        {{COPYRIGHT}}
    </text>

</svg>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">

  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="bgGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
      <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#1A1A2E"/>
      <stop offset="50%" style="stop-color:#16213E"/>
      <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#0F0F1A"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="accentGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#D97757"/>
      <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#E8956F"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <radialGradient id="glowOrange" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="50%">
      <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#D97757;stop-opacity:0.2"/>
      <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#D97757;stop-opacity:0"/>
    </radialGradient>
    <radialGradient id="glowBlue" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="50%">
      <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#4A90D9;stop-opacity:0.15"/>
      <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#4A90D9;stop-opacity:0"/>
    </radialGradient>
  </defs>

  <!-- Dark background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#bgGradient)"/>

  <!-- Grid decoration -->
  <line x1="0" y1="180" x2="1280" y2="180" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.02" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="0" y1="360" x2="1280" y2="360" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.02" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="0" y1="540" x2="1280" y2="540" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.02" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="320" y1="0" x2="320" y2="720" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.02" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="640" y1="0" x2="640" y2="720" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.02" stroke-width="1"/>
  <line x1="960" y1="0" x2="960" y2="720" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.02" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- Glow effects -->
  <ellipse cx="200" cy="150" rx="250" ry="180" fill="url(#glowBlue)"/>
  <ellipse cx="1080" cy="580" rx="280" ry="200" fill="url(#glowOrange)"/>

  <!-- Neural net decoration -->
  <path d="M150,120 Q260,80 360,160" stroke="#4A90D9" stroke-opacity="0.3" stroke-width="1" fill="none"/>
  <path d="M920,560 Q1020,510 1100,580" stroke="#4A90D9" stroke-opacity="0.3" stroke-width="1" fill="none"/>
  <circle cx="150" cy="120" r="4" fill="#4A90D9" fill-opacity="0.5"/>
  <circle cx="360" cy="160" r="6" fill="#4A90D9" fill-opacity="0.5"/>
  <circle cx="1100" cy="580" r="7" fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.6"/>

  <!-- Page label -->
  <text x="640" y="44" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="500" fill="#D97757" letter-spacing="3">KEY TAKEAWAYS</text>

  <!-- Title -->
  <text x="640" y="88" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="26" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">RL-Based Dialogue Control Opens Path to Production-Ready TA-LLMs</text>

  <!-- Separator -->
  <rect x="490" y="100" width="300" height="3" fill="url(#accentGradient)" rx="1.5"/>

  <!-- ===== 5 TAKEAWAY CARDS — 2 rows: 3 top + 2 bottom ===== -->

  <!-- Card 1: MDP Formulation -->
  <rect x="60" y="118" width="370" height="155" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.06" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.12" stroke-width="1" rx="10"/>
  <rect x="60" y="118" width="370" height="5" fill="#4A90D9" rx="4"/>
  <use data-icon="database" x="78" y="134" width="22" height="22" fill="#4A90D9"/>
  <text x="110" y="151" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">1. MDP Formulation Enables Systematic Pairing</text>
  <text x="78" y="178" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.85">5-state model (Initial → ... → Complete) defines</text>
  <text x="78" y="198" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.85">exactly which trajectories are correct or incorrect</text>
  <text x="78" y="218" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.85">for each of the 3 query types.</text>
  <text x="78" y="260" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#4A90D9">→ Principled preference learning framework</text>

  <!-- Card 2: Automatic Dataset -->
  <rect x="455" y="118" width="370" height="155" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.06" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.12" stroke-width="1" rx="10"/>
  <rect x="455" y="118" width="370" height="5" fill="#10B981" rx="4"/>
  <use data-icon="circle-checkmark" x="473" y="134" width="22" height="22" fill="#10B981"/>
  <text x="505" y="151" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981">2. Automatic Dataset — No Human Labels</text>
  <text x="473" y="178" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.85">10 pair types across 3 query categories are</text>
  <text x="473" y="198" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.85">generated programmatically from MDP definitions.</text>
  <text x="473" y="218" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.85">Scales without annotation cost or human effort.</text>
  <text x="473" y="260" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#10B981">→ Replicable pipeline for any TA-LLM dataset</text>

  <!-- Card 3: DPO Complements SFT -->
  <rect x="850" y="118" width="370" height="155" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.06" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.12" stroke-width="1" rx="10"/>
  <rect x="850" y="118" width="370" height="5" fill="#D97757" rx="4"/>
  <use data-icon="triangle-exclamation" x="868" y="134" width="22" height="22" fill="#D97757"/>
  <text x="900" y="151" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#D97757">3. DPO Complements SFT — Not Replaces It</text>
  <text x="868" y="178" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.85">DPO-only performs poorly (LLaMA Slot: 0.056).</text>
  <text x="868" y="198" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.85">SFT + DiaTool-DPO achieves best Macro Avg</text>
  <text x="868" y="218" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.85">across all three model sizes (3.1B and 8B).</text>
  <text x="868" y="260" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#D97757">→ Two-stage training is essential</text>

  <!-- Card 4: Largest Gains -->
  <rect x="160" y="290" width="380" height="155" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.06" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.12" stroke-width="1" rx="10"/>
  <rect x="160" y="290" width="380" height="5" fill="#D97757" rx="4"/>
  <use data-icon="arrow-trend-up" x="178" y="306" width="22" height="22" fill="#D97757"/>
  <text x="210" y="323" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#D97757">4. Largest Gains in Slot & Rejection</text>
  <text x="178" y="350" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.85">LLaMA-3-8B: Slot +43.5% (0.639→0.917),</text>
  <text x="178" y="370" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.85">Relevance +10.5% (0.826→0.913) over SFT-only.</text>
  <text x="178" y="390" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.85">Macro Avg reaches 0.904 — near GPT-4o level.</text>
  <text x="178" y="432" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#D97757">→ 94.8% info gathering, 91% tool rejection</text>

  <!-- Card 5: Language-agnostic -->
  <rect x="740" y="290" width="380" height="155" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.06" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.12" stroke-width="1" rx="10"/>
  <rect x="740" y="290" width="380" height="5" fill="#10B981" rx="4"/>
  <use data-icon="globe" x="758" y="306" width="22" height="22" fill="#10B981"/>
  <text x="790" y="323" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981">5. Language-Agnostic & Production-Ready</text>
  <text x="758" y="350" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.85">Primary experiments in Korean; method generalizes</text>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

Welcome to this presentation on DiaTool-DPO — a novel approach to improving tool-augmented LLM dialogue through Direct Preference Optimization. Today we'll cover how framing TA-LLM interactions as a Markov Decision Process enables automatic construction of preference pairs that teach models when to ask questions, when to call tools, and when to reject out-of-scope requests.

Key points: (1) Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2504.02882 (2) Core contribution: MDP + DPO applied to tool-augmented dialogue (3) Outcome: Near GPT-4o performance on smaller open-source models
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_problem_motivation

[Transition] Before we dive into the solution, let's understand the problem that DiaTool-DPO addresses.

Tool-augmented LLMs face three critical failure modes when trained only with SFT. First, hallucinated tool invocations — the model fabricates missing parameter values instead of asking. [Pause] Second, missing slot-filling — the model skips clarification and calls a tool with incomplete arguments. Third, failed rejection — when no matching tool exists, the model still attempts a call rather than declining gracefully.

[Data] SFT copies correct expert trajectories only. There are no negative examples, no contrastive signal — the model never sees what "wrong" dialogue looks like. DiaTool-DPO closes this gap by pairing correct and incorrect trajectories automatically.

Key points: (1) Three failure modes all stem from SFT's lack of negative signal (2) DPO provides contrastive learning from chosen/rejected trajectory pairs (3) Pairs are constructed automatically — no human labeling needed
Duration: 2 minutes

[Pause] Each type has a distinct "wrong" trajectory that teaches a specific lesson: Type 1 rejects must prevent redundant questioning, Type 2 completions must prevent slot hallucination, and Type 3 acceptances must prevent hallucinated tool calls.

Key points: (1) Query type determines correct trajectory — wrong path = preference pair opportunity (2) DPO lessons: prevent redundant QA, prevent hallucination, teach rejection (3) Classification is automatic via MDP state analysis
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 05_dataset_construction

[Transition] Now let's see how these three query types translate into a 10-pair-type preference dataset.

For each query type and trajectory combination, we construct chosen (correct) and rejected (incorrect) trajectory pairs. For Type 1: the chosen path skips slot-filling, while rejected paths add unnecessary S2 loops. For Type 2: chosen paths include the required slot-filling rounds, while rejected paths jump straight to tool calls — slot hallucination. For Type 3: the model must learn to self-loop in S1, with rejected paths showing incorrect tool invocations. [Data] The total dataset covers easy pairs (2,089 Type 1/2 examples) and harder pairs (562–2,530 examples) across all three query categories.

The critical point: all of this is generated automatically from the MDP state definitions. Zero human annotation required.

Key points: (1) 10 pair types covering all query type/trajectory combinations (2) Difficulty levels: easy pairs use single-step trajectory deviations, hard pairs use multi-step ones (3) No human labeling — fully automatic construction
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 06_benchmark_results

[Transition] With the dataset constructed, let's examine the results on FunctionChat-Bench.

The main finding is clear: SFT + DiaTool-DPO achieves the best Macro Average across all three model sizes. [Data] For Prop.-8B, SFT + DPO reaches 0.868 Macro Avg versus 0.856 for SFT-only. For Prop.-3.1B, 0.818 versus 0.791. And for LLaMA-3-8B, 0.904 versus 0.816 — an improvement of more than ten percentage points. [Pause] The DPO-only baseline performs poorly across the board — LLaMA-3-8B DPO-only Macro Avg is only 0.199, confirming that DPO cannot replace SFT.

Key points: (1) SFT + DiaTool-DPO wins Macro Avg for all three model sizes (2) Slot and Relevance metrics show the largest improvements (3) DPO-only is insufficient — two-stage training required
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 07_llama_performance_gains

[Transition] The LLaMA-3-8B results deserve special attention — they show the most dramatic improvements.

When DiaTool-DPO is added to SFT for LLaMA-3-8B, Slot accuracy jumps from 0.639 to 0.917 — a 43.5% relative improvement. [Data] To put that in context: slot accuracy of 0.639 means the model is failing to ask follow-up questions in more than a third of incomplete queries. At 0.917, that failure rate drops dramatically. Relevance — tool call rejection accuracy — improves from 0.826 to 0.913, a 10.5% gain. Overall Macro Average reaches 0.904, approaching GPT-4o's 94.8% information gathering and 91% tool rejection benchmark.

Key points: (1) +43.5% Slot accuracy is the most dramatic individual metric gain (2) Relevance +10.5% shows DPO teaches out-of-scope rejection (3) Near GPT-4o performance achievable on smaller open-source models
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 08_key_takeaways

[Transition] Let me close with five key takeaways from DiaTool-DPO.

First, the MDP formulation is the foundational contribution — it enables systematic generation of preference pairs without manual effort. Second, the dataset is fully automatic — 10 pair types, scaling with data volume, no annotation cost. Third, DPO complements rather than replaces SFT — the two-stage approach is essential. Fourth, the gains are concentrated where TA-LLMs most frequently fail: slot-filling and tool rejection. And fifth, the method is language-agnostic — tested in Korean with generalization to English, making it applicable to any production TA-LLM system.

[Pause] For practitioners: this approach provides a clear recipe for improving dialogue control in tool-augmented systems without expensive human annotation pipelines.

Key points: (1) MDP + automatic pairs = principled preference learning for TA-LLMs (2) Two-stage SFT + DPO training is the recommended deployment pattern (3) Language-agnostic; generalizes beyond Korean to any TA-LLM application
Duration: 2 minutes
